instruction: I have jotted down my amazon shopping list in simple_note. Reset my amazon cart to have as many products in as many quantities from this list as available, and tell me its total cost. In calculating the total cost (i) only include the available items, and (ii) include tax, but not delivery fees as I will be using prime later.
notes: Two-app task (simple_note + amazon). The shopping list is found via simple_note.search_notes and read via show_note (sets shopping-list-known); each list entry is modeled as a placeholder product (list-product-1..3) with a search query (its name on the note) resolved by amazon.search_products (known-id) and checked for stock/price by amazon.show_product (availability-known). World facts (purchasable ?p ?q) encode the quantity the store can supply for an entry, i.e. min(requested, inventory_quantity); an out-of-stock entry (list-product-3) has no purchasable fact and therefore can never be added, but the goal still demands it be checked. The cart is reset with clear_cart (allowed once, required before any add) and products are added with add_product_to_cart; show_cart yields the cart total (tax included, delivery fee excluded) and every add/clear invalidates cart-total-known so show_cart must follow the last add. complete_task carries the total as its answer; product-specific in-cart facts live only in the problem goal since the domain cannot name problem objects, but ordering is still enforced because every other action requires (not (task-completed)). The number of list entries, which are available, and their quantities are placeholders to be adapted to the actual note content at runtime.
